version.changelog: Add explicit secret-handling guidance and verify the skill contains no hardcoded local paths or published credential values.

llm.summary: The skill matches its Raindrop.io bookmark-management purpose, but it handles OAuth tokens and destructive account actions with too little protection or warning.

dimensions.detail: Network access to official Raindrop.io API and OAuth endpoints, local input/output files, and Raindrop credentials are proportionate for this integration; no unrelated network destinations or broad local indexing were found.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains Markdown documentation and a local Python CLI; I found no install hook, background service, tool hijacking, remote code retrieval, or automatic execution path.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill advertises update and delete operations for bookmarks and collections, and the script executes those account mutations directly without confirmation, preview, or prominent destructive-action warnings.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: OAuth completion and refresh save client secrets, access tokens, and refresh tokens to a local env file by default without enforcing restrictive file permissions, and they also print the full token response to stdout.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The CLI’s Raindrop.io API access, bookmark import/export, collection management, OAuth flow, and local credential use are coherent with the stated bookmark-manager purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving this skill access to your Raindrop account. Prefer environment variables or a short-lived test token, avoid passing secrets on the command line, check permissions on any ~/.openclaw/raindrop.env file, and be careful with delete/update/import commands because they can change or remove account data without an extra confirmation step.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: Credential references are expected for a Raindrop API/OAuth manager and the docs tell users not to publish real secrets, but the implementation still stores and emits sensitive token values in ways users may not expect.
[AE1] unexpected: I fully inspected the referenced SKILL.md, references, and script files in the workspace, so the scanner’s partial-inspection concern does not hold for this adjudication.
[TM1] expected: The DELETE endpoints are normal Raindrop API capabilities for the stated manager role, not evidence of tool abuse by themselves; the concern is missing confirmation or safety guidance around destructive use.
[LP3] unexpected: The skill does not declare explicit permission boundaries, which matters because it uses credentials, filesystem I/O, and network calls, although those capabilities are mostly purpose-aligned.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The concerns about under-warned destructive operations and default plaintext OAuth persistence are supported by the artifact and contribute to the Review verdict.
[E1] expected: External transmission is to documented Raindrop.io API and OAuth endpoints needed for the skill’s purpose; I found no unrelated exfiltration destination.
[TT2] expected: Writing exported bookmark data or import results to a user-specified output file is expected for import/export workflows.
[T09] unexpected: The static findings about unprotected plaintext token persistence and unredacted token output are supported by the script; the OAuth state/PKCE issue is lower-risk but still a security-quality gap.
